slice.leaf: deterministic orphan-retention model for checkpoint-first/pointer-last CAS persistence
slice.question: Can orphan accumulation be reduced without deleting any checkpoint still reachable from current or immediately previous LATEST, under interruption and stale-writer traces?

model.objects: immutable role-local checkpoints plus a CAS-updated LATEST pointer; failed/interrupted candidate writes may leave unreachable orphan checkpoints
model.reachability: a checkpoint is protected when reachable from the current LATEST target or the immediately previous confirmed LATEST target; predecessor links, when present, are included transitively
model.confirmed_generation: increments only after a successful LATEST CAS and exact readback; failed candidate writes do not advance it

candidates.A_never_delete: Append-only retention; never delete any checkpoint.
candidates.B_age_only: Delete checkpoints after an age threshold without consulting current/previous LATEST reachability.
candidates.C_reachability_two_confirmations: A checkpoint is cleanup-eligible only after it is unreachable from both current and immediately previous LATEST and has remained unreachable across two successful confirmed pointer generations; no automatic orphan adoption.

steps: write orphan o1 as candidate child of c0
later successfully commit c1 then c2
deterministic_traces.B: not falsified by this trace alone; behavior depends only on elapsed age and ignores authority
deterministic_traces.C: safe; o1 remains protected from cleanup until two successful pointer generations have observed it unreachable, then becomes eligible

steps: stale writer based on c0 writes s1
later successfully commit c2 then c3
deterministic_traces.B: cannot distinguish s1 from an old still-authoritative checkpoint by age alone
deterministic_traces.C: safe within model; rejected s1 never becomes reachable and is eligible only after two later confirmed generations

steps: candidate writes may occur but no LATEST CAS succeeds
deterministic_traces.A: safe; orphan count can grow without bound
deterministic_traces.B: FALSIFIED: an age-only sweeper can delete c0 while current LATEST still points to c0, creating a dangling authoritative pointer
deterministic_traces.C: safe; no successful pointer generation means no cleanup eligibility matures, so canonical state is preserved; orphan count can still grow without bound

steps: orphan o1 is unreachable at confirmed generation g
successful LATEST updates establish g+1 and g+2
o1 remains unreachable from current and previous LATEST at both confirmations
deterministic_traces.C: o1 may be deleted after g+2 without deleting any checkpoint reachable from current or immediately previous LATEST

A_never_delete.bounded_orphan_storage: FAIL without an external bound on failed writes
A_never_delete.conflict_duplication_risk: low for deletion, high storage growth
A_never_delete.expected_completion_time: immediate but does not solve retention growth

B_age_only.falsifier: pointer_stuck_no_confirmed_progress can delete the checkpoint still named by current LATEST
B_age_only.conflict_duplication_risk: high because time is not authority

C_reachability_two_confirmations.safety: PASS in all tested interruption/stale-writer traces
C_reachability_two_confirmations.bounded_orphan_storage: PARTIAL: bounds cleanup eligibility by successful pointer generations, but cannot provide an absolute orphan-count bound when confirmed pointer progress is zero
C_reachability_two_confirmations.integration_cost: medium; requires reachability bookkeeping and two confirmed pointer-generation observations
C_reachability_two_confirmations.conflict_duplication_risk: low in tested model because authority is pointer/reachability-based, not wall-clock-based
C_reachability_two_confirmations.expected_completion_time: two successful pointer generations before an unreachable checkpoint becomes cleanup-eligible

slice.candidate_revision: Use reachability-plus-two-confirmed-generation retention as the only cleanup candidate from this slice; keep never-delete as the fail-safe fallback. Reject age-only deletion. Do not claim absolute orphan boundedness: with zero confirmed pointer progress, safe cleanup intentionally stops.
slice.tested_scope: Deterministic role-local model of immutable checkpoint files and one CAS-updated LATEST pointer, including interruption before pointer CAS, stale-writer CAS rejection, zero confirmed progress, and two later successful pointer generations. No live deletion was performed; no claim is made for multi-file atomicity, branch deletion semantics, transports other than this checkpoint/pointer model, or storage bounds during indefinite pointer stagnation.
slice.negative_result: No retention rule based only on wall-clock/file age is safe in this model because authority can remain on an old checkpoint indefinitely. Reachability-based cleanup is safe in tested traces but cannot by itself cap orphan creation while LATEST never advances.

phase1_constraints.quota_note: This slice used only deterministic reasoning over role-local repository-state semantics; no hosted runner, Codespaces, artifact/LFS/package, external model/API credit, or paid compute is required.

slice.conflict_check: No O/O-derived, other-worker, downstream, legacy, aggregate-ledger, other-role receipt/config, or unrelated semantic input was used. No scheduler or protected-primary state was read or mutated.

frontier: Bound orphan creation rather than relying on deletion: test a deterministic per-parent attempt key/path derived from current LATEST blob SHA plus intended next logical revision, with normalized deterministic payload and create/CAS collision semantics, so repeated failed attempts from the same parent cannot create an unbounded sequence of distinct orphans.
After that, test interruption/rate-limit recovery without same-run retry, preserving checkpoint-first/pointer-last authority and exact-content duplicate idempotence.
exact_continuation: Next invocation, after manifest/RUN_LIFECYCLE-first bootstrap and exact authority freeze, read LATEST and this r173 checkpoint only as needed, then execute exactly one bounded deterministic idempotency-key model leaf. Compare unique-per-attempt orphan paths against a deterministic path keyed by {parent LATEST blob SHA, intended logical revision}; require that repeated attempts from the same frozen parent either exact-match the existing candidate or stop diagnostically, never auto-adopt mismatched content, never spawn a second orphan path, and never overwrite a reachable checkpoint. Falsify the design if an interruption/stale-writer trace can create more than one distinct orphan for the same parent or can mutate current authority.
